text:
Jacob Trouba is in his first season in San Jose, his fourth NHL stop after Winnipeg, the Rangers (where he wore the C) and Anaheim. At 32, he is the kind of player a young team leans on, playing more than 22 minutes a night as the Sharks have started to find some wins.

His numbers fit the role. He has 2 goals and 11 points in 23 games, close to what our talent range expects, and his finishing is about normal. At five-on-five, San Jose has had about 46% of the chance quality with him out there, which sounds poor until you see the team does worse without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows both sides of his game. He is hard to beat at his own blue line, stopping 16% of the entries aimed at him against a typical 11%. But only 28% of his exits kept the puck, so watch for clears off the glass under a heavy forecheck. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season; his value to this team may be more about the minutes he soaks up.
headline: Jacob Trouba brings a veteran's minutes to a young Sharks team
